chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from the one who mentioned it, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim al-Ja'fari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed the scholar, when he does not act according to his knowledge, his admonition slides off hearts just as rain slides off smooth rock.

key_terms.الصَّفَا: Smooth rock — used here metaphorically for a surface from which water cannot be absorbed; implies hardened, impenetrable resistance
key_terms.الْعَالِم: The scholar — one who possesses religious knowledge and bears the obligation to embody it
key_terms.مَوْعِظَة: Admonition/exhortation — moral guidance, advice intended to move the heart to action

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Sadiq say about scholars who do not practice what they preach?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) emphasizes that a scholar who does not practice what he preaches loses all moral authority — his words fail to penetrate the hearts of his listeners. The vivid simile of rain sliding off smooth rock conveys that mere verbal admonition, without accompanying deeds, has no lasting effect. This teaching was especially directed toward religious authorities and scholars in early Islamic society who bore a social responsibility to lead by example.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ali Bin Muhammad Al Qasany, from the one who mentioned it, from Abdullah Bin Al Qasim Al Ja’fary, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘
The scholar, when he does not act for (performing) his deed, his advice would slide off from the hearts just as the rain drops slide off from the rock’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani from one he mentioned from ‘Abdallah ibn Qasim al-Ja’fari from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following. “
If a scholar preaches and does not practice his words bounce away from the hearts of the audience like rains that bounce away off the rocks.”
